properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Generated 2026-09-02.

proj:chama asked for a new edge type to say "this open decision determines whether this constraint can be met". THE EDGE EXISTS — `Constraint --GOVERNED_BY--> Decision` — and they could not find it, because `describe_schema` ranks by endpoint enumeration and GOVERNED_BY is `*` on both sides deliberately. It falls into the alphabetical wildcard pile for EVERY pair in the design. They reached for BLOCKS and buried the meaning in an `evidence` string.

**THE PREVIOUS TWO INSTANCES WERE FIXED BY ENUMERATING AN ENDPOINT** — VERIFIES in #112, and CONSTRAINS' source on 2026-08-08 after `describe_schema{DesignRule, Component}` returned zero exact matches. THAT REPAIR IS UNAVAILABLE HERE and schema/core.yaml says why in its own words: narrowing a wildcard is a consumer-facing break, and "what a rule limits" is genuinely open. GOVERNED_BY's openness is CORRECT. So the third instance of a class cannot take the fix that closed the first two, which is the signal that the class was mis-stated.

**THE RESTATEMENT: the ranking criterion is not the thing it is presented as.** `exact` / `half_exact` measures HOW NARROWLY AN EDGE IS DECLARED. It is presented to the caller as how well the edge MODELS THEIR PAIR. Those coincide for edges whose narrowness is meaningful and come apart exactly for edges whose openness is meaningful — and the second set includes GOVERNED_BY, CAUSES, RISKS, MITIGATES, BLOCKS, CONTRADICTS, OBSOLETES: most of the semantic vocabulary.

🛑 **A THIRD REPORTER, AND THE MOST EXPENSIVE — AND IT IS WORSE THAN UNDER-RANKING.** dev_storyflow, 2026-08-23, needed to say "this repair invalidates that check's last run". They ran the discovery tool, exactly as instructed, and reported: *"`describe_schema(from=Constraint, to=Verification)` returns 0 exact matches ... the two half-exact options (`CONSTRAINS`, `CALIBRATED_AGAINST`) model something else. The nearest honest assertion available is `CONTRADICTS` ... It works, and it is obviously a stand-in."* They drew the stand-in and wrote *"an `INVALIDATES_RUN` ... would say the true thing."*

**`INVALIDATES` IS EXACTLY THAT EDGE.** Its hint names their case verbatim — *"a repair against the check that found it ... Draw it from whatever recorded the work (a Constraint, a ChangeEvent, a Decision) to whatever recorded the finding (a Verification, a TemporalFact)."* Re-measured 2026-09-02: it comes back **eleventh, in the wildcard pile**, while `CONSTRAINS` and `CALIBRATED_AGAINST` — which model something else, as they correctly judged — are PROMOTED ABOVE IT as `half_exact`.

⭐ **SO THE DEFECT IS SHARPER THAN "THE RIGHT ANSWER IS UNDER-RANKED": THE RANKING ACTIVELY PROMOTES WRONG EDGES ABOVE THE RIGHT ONE.** chama's case had 0 half-exact and a flat pile; this one had two half-exact hits, both wrong, sitting above the true answer. A caller who trusts the ranking is worse off than one who ignores it.
⚠️ BOUND, and it matters: `INVALIDATES` merged 2026-08-23 (#321) and released in v0.40.0 (2026-08-26). Their entry is that evening and they could not read their version, so it very likely was not in their build and they cannot be said to have missed it. What IS established is that the ranking would hide it from them TODAY. They also attached a cost — "it cost 49 days" on one blocked item — but that cost belongs to the missing capability, not provably to the ranking.

IDEAS TURNED OVER, none preferred:
· **A `deliberately_open` marker per edge type**, so describe_schema can distinguish "open because nobody thought about it" from "open because anything may be governed" and rank the second above the wildcard pile. ⭐ The only option that also separates the two replies below.
· **Rank by USAGE in this graph** — a pair actually drawn is evidence of a modelled fit that no declaration carries. ⚠️ It reports what people DO rather than what is RIGHT, so an established wrong habit would rank above a correct unused edge.
· **Let the hint declare its own pairs** in text, and rank on that, changing nothing structural.
· **Nothing structural: fix the NOTE.** It already says "prefer leaving the edge out to asserting one that is wrong" — it could also say "an edge open on both sides may still be the modelled fit; read the hints, do not read the ranking as an answer." ⚠️ Does NOT stop wrong edges being promoted above right ones.
· **Do nothing.** ⚠️ Now three reporters across two projects, and one of them acted on the ranking and drew a stand-in edge they themselves called wrong.

⭐ **THE SHARPEST FORM, MEASURED 2026-09-02 BY ACCIDENT.** Two calls the same day:
· `describe_schema{Decision, Constraint}` → 0 exact, 0 half-exact, 17 wildcards. **The right edge EXISTS and is in that pile.**
· `describe_schema{Decision, Question}` → 0 exact, 0 half-exact, 17 wildcards. **No right edge existed at all** — the genuinely missing vocabulary that became `ANSWERS`.
**THE TWO REPLIES ARE THE SAME SHAPE AND THE CALLER CANNOT TELL WHICH SITUATION THEY ARE IN.** "The answer is in this list and I am not ranking it" and "there is no answer, ask for one" are opposite facts requiring opposite actions, rendered identically.

⚠️ WHAT NOBODY HAS MEASURED: how many of the ~18 wildcard edge types carry real semantics, and how often an agent picks a wrong edge because the right one was unranked. Three observed instances now, from three reporters. `dec:edge-orthogonality` sets the bar any answer must clear — a vocabulary distinction earns its keep ONLY IF A COMPUTATION READS IT.
properties.name: SETTLED on Anthony's word 2026-09-02 — an edge type declares when its wildcard is DELIBERATE, and describe_schema ranks those above the noise instead of burying them with the accidental ones
properties.rationale:
Worth recording rather than acting on because the finding REFUTES a feature request, and that is the expensive kind to lose. Without this node the next reader meets chama's report, agrees a Decision→Constraint edge is missing, and adds vocabulary for a relation that already exists — making the discovery problem worse by putting two edges where one was already unfindable.

The fourth option costs a sentence and is available immediately whatever is decided about the rest.
